liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Easy Wind** (3 reviews): Reviewer also praises the Easy Wind as great; Starts out stumbling, then delivers sweet harmonica and a mind-boggling guitar excursion [6][9][13]
- **Till The Morning Comes** (3 reviews): Band reportedly wasn't impressed with it, but reviewer finds it fine, given it was played only a handful of times; Reviewer calls this their favorite recording of this rarely played song and wishes it were played more, even as an opener [10][11][15]
- **Big Railroad Blues** (1 review, 1 other source): Reviewer's high rating is due to this Big Railroad Blues; Opening seconds are clipped; this version has some novel lyrics [4][10]
- **The Frozen Logger** (1 review): Reviewer considers this the best Frozen Logger performance [6]
- **Friend Of The Devil** (1 review): Reviewer singles out the electric version of Friend of the Devil [10]
- **New Minglewood Blues** (1 review): Slightly slower in tempo, resembling the band's first album version [15]
- **Beat It On Down The Line** (1 other source): This version gets four beats [4]

## Setlist highlights

- **The Frozen Logger**: rare: 9 archived performances [17]
- **Till The Morning Comes**: rare: 6 archived performances [17]

## The recordings

- **gd1970-12-26.sbd.ashley-field.34031.sbeok.flac16** (recommended): soundboard; 20 songs; 137 min; rated 4.45/5 by 11 [1]. Said about its sound: Reviewer finds the sound unique and crisp, with Jerry's Gibson SG prominent; some vocal harmonies are strained; Reviewer hears a definite improvement over other Internet Archive copies of this show [15][16]
- **gd70-12-26.sbd.miller.22369.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 20 songs; 137 min; rated 4.23/5 by 13 [2]. Said about its sound: Reviewer notes the soundboard recording has a few sound problems; Some songs drag slowly; reviewer sped up several tracks by roughly 3 to 11 percent to improve them; Recording sounds a bit slow [6][12][13][14]
- **gd1970-12-26.sbd.lai.7465.sbefail.shnf**: soundboard; 18 songs; 105 min; rated 4.4/5 by 5 [3]
- **gd1970-12-26.sbd.unknown.14124.sbefail.shnf**: soundboard; 18 songs; 107 min; rated 4.33/5 by 3 [4]

## Around the show

- Some songs start clunky but pay off with strong vocal intensity and rewarding jams [9]
- Sounds from Workingman's Dead and American Beauty came together only during a short window [12]
- Reviewer considers this the most funky-sounding show by the band, and a personal all-time favorite [14]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1970-12-26.sbd.ashley-field.34031.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Jay Ashley and Gary Field; source: Bertha Remaster of the Master Reel/Cassette source (SHN ID 22369) [1]. Also: Friend Of The Devil was remastered with the Bertha workstation, completed April 4, 2006, after minor cleanup; DVD audio extraction and FLAC compression done by Gary Field on 4/20/2006; Charlie patched the recording [1]
- **gd70-12-26.sbd.miller.22369.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: Soundboard [2]. Also: Lineage: soundboard to master reel, then unknown step, then DAT, then SHN; Patches appear in Easy Wind, Till The Morning Comes, Truckin', Black Peter, Morning Dew and China Cat into Rider [2]
- **gd1970-12-26.sbd.lai.7465.sbefail.shnf**: transferred by Mike Lai and Wayne Gucwa; source: sdb>>R>>pcm>>cd [3]. Also: Seeded to etree and further by Mike Lai; thanks go to Wayne Gucwa for sharing [3]
- **gd1970-12-26.sbd.unknown.14124.sbefail.shnf**: transferred by Unknown; source: SBD>??(maybe 2 reel gens)>PCM>WAV>CDR>EAC>SHN [4]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead Legion Stadium - December 26, 1970](https://www.dead.net/show/december-26-1970) [18]
